Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we agreed on. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable latency and token costs during peak batch jobs (nightly enrichment spikes).
- Need tenant isolation for PII-sensitive models (compliance + auditability).
- Current infra is a mix of OpenAI managed endpoints (for experiments) and an on-prem GPU pool for heavier workloads - switching between them is operationally painful.

Current stack / constraints:
- Model runtime: mixture of open models and a proprietary ranker you run in-house.
- Peak pattern: baseline ~60 TPS during daytime traffic; nightly batch bursts up to ~220 TPS for ~10-minute windows.
- Procurement: finance wants a 30-60 day review and prefers a committed monthly cost for predictability.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit:
- Predictable p95 latency under committed load (target: p95 < 150ms for online requests).
- Reserved GPU pools with single-tenant isolation for sensitive workloads.
- Autoscale/burst policy to handle nightly spikes without impacting SLAs.
- Clear unit economics (per-token cost + reserved capacity amortization) for finance to review.

Next steps we agreed on:
1) Redwood: share an initial Dedicated sizing + pricing workbook and our standard security questionnaire (attached).
2) Rishi: validate the throughput assumptions and propose a node/configuration that covers baseline + burst with autoscale behavior.
3) Sofia + Carlos: share any procurement/contract constraints or required terms we should be aware of.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive (SE + infra) next week to go over perf expectations and networking (we suggested Wed 3/25).

I've attached an initial pricing workbook and our security questionnaire for your team to review.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — quick tech notes after a preliminary look:

Observation & recommendation:
- Baseline: 60 TPS steady state - recommend reserving a pool sized for ~1.25x baseline to keep headroom (suggestion: 3 GPU nodes with 40-60 concurrent inference slots each depending on model).
- Burst: for 200-220 TPS bursts lasting 5-15 minutes, recommend autoscale policy that allows +2 nodes on burst with aggressive scale-up (30s) and 10-15 minute cool-down. This covers your worst-case bursts while keeping cost down.
- Cold-start: recommend pre-warming KV cache and keeping a small hot pool for large models; estimate cold-start latency can be brought down to ~200-300ms with pre-warm strategies (we'll need model sizes to refine).
- Isolation: offer single-tenant reservation for PII workloads; network-level VPC peering and KMS/HSM integration for key management. Monica — please add any SOC2 / audit log specifics.

Next steps I can take this afternoon:
- Produce a node-level config (GPU type + counts) and run a back-of-envelope cost amortization for monthly reserved pricing.
- Add autoscale policy details to the pricing workbook and mark assumptions.

I'll attach the suggested config sheet and the updated pricing workbook once I run numbers.
